intel_items.title: BIS interim final rule on remote access to advanced AI chips
intel_items.summary: BIS issued an interim final rule requiring a license to sell advanced chips to overseas data centers that supply significant computing volumes to firms headquartered in countries of concern, and to export advanced chips to companies headquartered in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil. Effective in 90 days. Thresholds must be confirmed from the Federal Register text.

sources.excerpt_note: Press release announcing the rule; full rule text not yet pulled.
Describes the license triggers and the five smuggling-risk countries.

intel_items.notes: The significant-volume threshold is a placeholder until the rule text is read.

intel_items.title: License applications must disclose IaaS remote end users
intel_items.summary: Since January 2026, license applications for advanced chips must list IaaS remote end users whose parent is headquartered in a listed country, and describe the consignee's KYC procedures.

sources.excerpt_note: Rule text on license review policy and remote end-user disclosure.

intel_items.title: BIS guidance on China-headquartered firms worldwide
intel_items.summary: BIS guidance said the November 2023 license requirement applies anywhere in the world when advanced chips go to China-headquartered firms or their subsidiaries.

sources.excerpt_note: Reports the guidance and its worldwide reach.

intel_items.title: Agencies have sought an Entity List designation for Megaspeed
intel_items.summary: Press reports that Megaspeed, a Singapore company with Malaysian and Indonesian subsidiaries, bought large volumes of advanced chips for Chinese customers; the company says its business is lawful. Treasury says several agencies have wanted it on the Entity List. It is not listed.

sources.excerpt_note: Quotes Treasury on the push to list Megaspeed.
